ruling: Setbacks for manufactured homes in a mobile home park. One sentence, printed once in each dimensional table and spanned by rowspan over every setback row, which is why it counts ten times. ruling: Conditional Uses. Every mention is the header of a zone's conditional list — "the following uses and their accessory uses are allowed subject to GMC Chapter 17.70" — and a fourplex is not on any of them. What is on the R-7.2 list is a "multi-household dwelling, five- to eight-unit building on a collector or minor arterial", beside churches, fire stations and nursing homes. Four units is one below the bottom of that range.

sample: (e) Exceptions to the minimum and maximum parking ratios may be granted pursuant to GMC Section 17.80.090 (Minor exception). Exceptions exceeding 25 percent of
ruling: Variances, reached from 17.48.030(2)(e): an exception to a minimum or maximum parking ratio above 25 percent goes through this chapter, below it through the minor exception at 17.80.090. Both are ways of asking to be let off a standard this screen holds the applicant to, so neither can make a lot fit that does not.

sample: At the time of construction, enlargement, or change of use of any structure or development subject to GMC Chapter 17.80 (Design Review), except as provided in t
ruling: Design Review, named in the opening sentence of both 17.48.030 and 17.48.040. It is the process a development goes through, not a dimension it has to meet, and the reading of which developments those sections reach is recorded in `defaults` rather than settled by fetching a procedure chapter. Nothing in 17.80 could add a number to a stall.

sample: (e) Exceptions to the minimum and maximum parking ratios may be granted pursuant to GMC Section 17.80.090 (Minor exception). Exceptions exceeding 25 percent of
ruling: Minor exception, the other half of 17.48.030(2)(e) and the only binding reference the parking chapter opened: an exception to a minimum or maximum parking ratio of 25 percent or less is granted through it, anything larger through the variance chapter. It stands beside the parking minimum and maximum because it can move both, and it moves them for an applicant who asks -- which is a thing a person does at a counter, not a thing a parcel is. A screen that granted itself exceptions would be reporting what could be argued for rather than what the code says.
